comment: Actionable SNPs with genotype interpretations. Each SNP maps a genotype to a list of edges in the Health Universe graph that should be amplified, suppressed, or context-flagged. We start with ~30 of the most consensus-backed clinical / lifestyle markers. The rest of the genome is ignored to avoid false-precision; expansion is a deliberate curation step.

TT.label: ε3/ε3 (most common, baseline risk)
TT.summary: Baseline APOE genotype. Standard dementia-risk profile.

CT.label: ε3/ε4 (one risk allele) — heterozygous
CT.summary: Single ε4 allele roughly doubles late-onset Alzheimer's risk vs ε3/ε3. Lifestyle interventions for dementia weight more heavily for you.

CC.label: ε4/ε4 (two risk alleles) — homozygous
CC.summary: Two ε4 alleles confer 8-12× higher Alzheimer's risk vs ε3/ε3. Dementia-prevention edges weight 2× in your plan; cardiovascular and metabolic prevention also matter more given the shared mechanism.

CC.label: ε3 or ε4 background
CC.summary: Required to be read together with rs429358 for full APOE genotype.

CT.label: ε2/ε3 (one protective allele)
CT.summary: ε2 may confer some protection against late-onset Alzheimer's but is also linked to higher risk of type III hyperlipidemia. Net effect is mixed.

TT.label: ε2/ε2 (two protective alleles, rare)
TT.summary: Roughly half the dementia risk of ε3/ε3 but a higher risk of dysbetalipoproteinemia. Clinical significance unclear without lipid panel.

GG.label: C/C wild-type
GG.summary: Normal MTHFR function. No dietary folate adjustment needed beyond normal recommendations.

AG.label: C/T heterozygous (~30% reduced enzyme activity)
AG.summary: Slightly less efficient folate metabolism. Methylated folate forms (5-MTHF) may be preferred over folic acid; check homocysteine.

AA.label: T/T homozygous (~70% reduced enzyme activity)
AA.summary: Significantly reduced folate metabolism. Methylated folate forms strongly preferred. Routine homocysteine monitoring useful — elevations linked to CVD and cognitive risk.

AT.label: A/T heterozygous
AT.summary: ~17% higher per-allele obesity risk. Exercise sensitivity for weight remains intact — physical activity offsets the genetic effect.

AA.label: A/A homozygous
AA.summary: ~70% higher obesity risk vs T/T. Lifestyle (especially exercise) appears to fully mitigate the variant's effect — weight control is harder but not predetermined.

II.label: I/I (insertion homozygous)
II.summary: Endurance-favoured genotype. Modest enrichment in elite endurance athletes.

ID.label: I/D heterozygous
ID.summary: Mixed phenotype. No meaningful clinical implications outside athletic context.

DD.label: D/D (deletion homozygous)
DD.summary: Power/strength-favoured genotype. Modest enrichment in sprinters and powerlifters.

GG.label: Val/Val wild-type
GG.summary: Standard BDNF secretion. Baseline cognition / mood profile.

AG.label: Val/Met heterozygous
AG.summary: ~30% reduced activity-dependent BDNF release. Aerobic exercise's pro-cognitive effects matter more for offsetting this.

AA.label: Met/Met homozygous
AA.summary: More substantial BDNF reduction. Stress-resilience and learning-related interventions weighted higher.

GT.label: A/C heterozygous
GT.summary: Mild reduction in MTHFR activity at this position. Combined effect with C677T (rs1801133) matters more than each alone.

GG.label: C/C homozygous
GG.summary: ~30-40% reduced enzyme activity. Combined with C677T heterozygosity has a larger effect; check homocysteine.

GG.label: Lactase non-persistent (lactose intolerant)
GG.summary: Lactase production declines after weaning. Most adults globally have this genotype. Symptomatic intolerance varies — try dairy-free for 4 weeks if GI symptoms.

AG.label: Heterozygous (lactase persistent)
AG.summary: Lactase persistence — should tolerate dairy normally as an adult.

AA.label: Homozygous lactase persistent
AA.summary: Strongest lactase persistence. Dairy is well-tolerated.

AA.label: Fast caffeine metaboliser
AA.summary: Caffeine is cleared quickly. Less likely to disrupt sleep from afternoon coffee; cardiovascular effects of high intake are smaller.

AC.label: Intermediate metaboliser
AC.summary: Average caffeine metabolism. Standard advice applies.

CC.label: Slow caffeine metaboliser
CC.summary: Caffeine lingers significantly longer. Higher cardiovascular risk from heavy intake; afternoon caffeine more likely to disrupt sleep. Cap at 1-2 cups, none after 12pm.

GT.label: Heterozygous (reduced excretion)
GT.summary: ~30% higher serum uric acid risk. Worth checking uric acid + considering gout-prevention edges.

TT.label: Homozygous (significantly reduced excretion)
TT.summary: Significantly higher gout risk. Limit fructose, alcohol, organ meats; check uric acid.

AG.label: A1/A2 heterozygous
AG.summary: ~30% reduced D2 receptor density. Some evidence for higher reward-seeking and addiction susceptibility, but effect size is small. Behavioural interventions remain the dominant lever.

AA.label: A1/A1 homozygous
AA.summary: Larger reduction in D2 density. Studies suggest moderately higher addiction risk; intentional dopamine-fasting / habit design may help, though evidence is mixed.

CC.label: R/R (alpha-actinin-3 expressed)
CC.summary: Power/sprint-favoured genotype. Disproportionately enriched in elite sprinters and powerlifters.

CT.label: R/X heterozygous
CT.summary: Mixed phenotype — most of the population. Both endurance and strength training respond normally.

TT.label: X/X (alpha-actinin-3 absent)
TT.summary: Endurance-favoured genotype. Slightly reduced sprint/power potential; endurance training response is normal to enhanced.

GG.label: G/G genotype
GG.summary: Some studies suggest stronger social-bonding response and stress recovery; effect sizes are small and culturally variable.

AA.label: A/A genotype
AA.summary: Some studies suggest reduced social-bonding response; clinical relevance is contested.

GG.label: PAV/PAV (taster)
GG.summary: Sensitive to bitter compounds. Likely to find cruciferous vegetables, dark chocolate, coffee, and brassicas more bitter than average.

AA.label: AVI/AVI (non-taster)
AA.summary: Reduced bitter sensitivity — bitter foods often more palatable.

GT.label: G/T heterozygous
GT.summary: ~30% higher likelihood of reaching extreme longevity in some populations. Modest effect; lifestyle dwarfs it.

GG.label: G/G homozygous
GG.summary: Roughly 3× higher likelihood of reaching 95+ in studied populations. Still small absolute effect; doesn't override lifestyle.

CT.label: C/T heterozygous
CT.summary: ~40% per-allele increase in T2D risk. Glycemic-control edges weight more heavily for you.

TT.label: T/T homozygous
TT.summary: ~2× T2D risk. Especially worth tracking HbA1c trajectory; lifestyle interventions for glycemic control are high-leverage.

CC.label: Arg/Arg
CC.summary: Stronger blood-pressure response to beta-blockers. May get more BP-lowering at lower doses.

GG.label: Gly/Gly
GG.summary: Reduced BP response to beta-blockers. May need higher doses or alternative classes.

GG.label: *1/*1 (extensive metaboliser)
GG.summary: Normal clopidogrel activation. Standard antiplatelet response.

AG.label: *1/*2 (intermediate metaboliser)
AG.summary: Reduced clopidogrel activation. Some guidelines recommend alternative antiplatelet (prasugrel/ticagrelor) for ACS.

AA.label: *2/*2 (poor metaboliser)
AA.summary: Significantly reduced clopidogrel activation. Strong guideline preference for alternative antiplatelet for ACS / PCI.

AC.label: *1/*3 heterozygous
AC.summary: ~40% lower warfarin clearance. Lower starting doses recommended; closer INR monitoring at initiation.

CC.label: *3/*3 homozygous (rare)
CC.summary: Very low warfarin clearance. Significantly lower doses + intensive INR monitoring required.

GG.label: Val/Val (warrior)
GG.summary: Faster dopamine clearance in prefrontal cortex. Tends toward better stress resilience but lower baseline reward sensitivity.

AA.label: Met/Met (worrier)
AA.summary: Slower dopamine clearance. Higher baseline cognitive performance under low stress; more anxiety-prone under high stress. Stress-management edges may matter more.
